analysis.title: Hotter US inflation strengthens the case for a December Fed hike
key_insights: October US CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month for headline and 0.3% for core, both 0.1ppt above consensus.
No year-on-year rates were published because the government shutdown meant no price data was collected in October 2025.
Details were mixed: new vehicle prices rose 0.2% m/m and used vehicle prices fell 1.2%, while medical care commodities rose 0.5%, transportation services rose 0.8% and shelter rose 0.3%.
Fed Governor Chris Waller said earlier on 10 November that he backs a 25bp hike in December and could opt for 50bp. After the CPI report the 10Y and 2Y Treasury yields were up 6bp and 13bp.
Markets now fully price a 25bp hike at the December Fed meeting, in line with ING's forecast, versus 20bp before Waller's comments.

Hopes of Middle East de-escalation have pushed retail gasoline below $4/gallon for the first time since mid-July. ING says this should drag on November headline inflation, but that data arrives the day after the December FOMC meeting.
ING does not forecast further hikes in 2027, citing cooling interest rate-sensitive sectors, housing costs, lower energy prices and weak wage growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Hot CPI and Waller's backing for a hike support a 25bp December move, which markets fully price and ING forecasts.
tension_points.bear_case: Waller said he could opt for a 50bp hike, and softer energy prices could let the Fed settle for 25bp.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Falling gasoline prices that lower November headline CPI, which the Fed may see in advance, would support only 25bp.
